correctness.rationale: Strong regularity and (n−d−1)μ=dm imply (dI−A)[(d−λ+μ)I+A]=μ(nI−J). Applied to the mean-zero edge dipole, this gives the unique mean-zero potential with levels 0, ±1/(μn), ±(m+μ)/(μn). Summing the four level-cut sizes with weights 1, 1, m+μ−1, m+μ−1 (before division by μn) gives the per-edge formula: each of the two wider cuts has size d(m+1)−2m−2 times the number of internal exclusive-neighbor edges on that side, and each singleton cut has size d. The diagonal is 2(m+μ)/(μn) and lies in [0,1], so taking the complementary projector adds the stated constant to every column sum; symmetry gives the row sums. Rook and Shrikhande have respectively 6 and 4 for τ_e on every edge, giving the exact four norms and gap 1/8. The shared parameters give the two nontrivial adjacency eigenvalues ±2 with multiplicities 6 and 9 by the trace. Independent incidence-SVD checks in both examples and K₃,₃ corroborate 105 columns (replay: python3 /workspace/evidence/review_checks.py 3); the exact general argument, not that finite check, establishes the result.
